source.section: Schedule SB (PDF page 1) and its Instructions: line 16 and its Caution (SB Instructions PDF page 7; Publication 126 PDF page 8 section 4.E(1); Publication 106 PDF page 4 section 3.C(1)); Form 1 lines 1-12 (Form 1 PDF page 1); Form 1 Instructions PDF page 15 line 8 and lines 10a-10b (PDF pages 15-16), PDF pages 35-37 2025 Standard Deduction Table (row named in worked), PDF page 15 line 12 with the PDF pages 38-43 Tax Table and PDF page 44 Tax Computation Worksheet; tax figured from the 2025 Tax Rate Schedules, Publication 106 PDF pages 6-7

worked: Married filing jointly, you 68, spouse 64: you IRA 20,000; spouse private pension 25,000; interest 30,000. Only you are 67: line 16 takes your own qualifying income 20,000 (under 24,000); the spouse's pension does not count while the spouse is under 67. The projection uses the 48,000 joint cap, but your income is under 24,000, so it gives the form's 20,000. Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = ira distribution (you) 20,000.00 + private pension (spouse) 25,000.00 + interest 30,000.00 = 75,000.00. Federal taxable income = 75,000.00 - standard deduction 31,500.00 + 1 x 1,600.00 = 41,900.00; the federal senior deduction is ignored. Form 1 line 1 federal AGI 75,000.00; line 2 Schedule I adjustments 0.00; line 3 75,000.00; line 4 additions 0.00; line 5 75,000.00. Schedule SB: line 16 retirement income subtraction: qualifying income you (age 68): IRA 20,000.00 = 20,000.00; smaller of 20,000.00 and the 48,000.00 cap = 20,000.00; line 50 total 20,000.00. Schedule SB line 17: federal AGI 75,000.00 is not less than 30,000.00, so no 5,000 subtraction. Form 1 line 6 20,000.00; line 7 Wisconsin income = 75,000.00 - 20,000.00 = 55,000.00. Line 8 standard deduction, 2025 Standard Deduction Table (Form 1 Instructions PDF page 35), row 55,000 to less than 55,500, column Married filing jointly: 19,762.00 (printed row, at least / less than / single / joint / separate / head of household: 55,000 / 55,500 / 9,276 / 19,762 / 3,651 / 9,482). Line 9 = 55,000.00 - 19,762.00 = 35,238.00. Line 10a 2 x 700 = 1,400.00; line 10b 1 x 250 = 250.00; line 10c 1,650.00. Line 11 taxable income = 35,238.00 - 1,650.00 = 33,588.00. Line 12 tax, Schedule B (joint) as numbers: 3.5% x 19,580.00 = 685.30 + 4.4% x 14,008.00 = 616.352; total 1,301.652, rounded once to 1,301.65. The Tax Table row 33,500 to 33,600 (PDF page 40) gives 1,300; expected keeps the schedule. Credits (lines 13-20, 30-35): none modelled; 0.00. State income tax 1,301.65.
accepted_approximations: The projection always takes the 24,000/48,000 subtraction for a person 67 or older, never the Wisconsin credits it bars (see not_modelled); a household whose credits are worth more would skip it.
